title: Practice 5: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: The pedestrian is crossing the road.
exercises.why: **переходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **переходить** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **перейти**. present: я перехожу́ · ты перехо́дишь · он перехо́дит · мы перехо́дим · вы перехо́дите · они перехо́дят. — Wiktionary, «переходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Студент переходит через улицу.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Танки медленно переходили через поле.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **выходит** (**выходить**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **доходит** (**доходить**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **приходит** (**приходить**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отвезу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **отвезти** (to take away (by vehicle), to drive away, to take (someone or something by vehicle)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отвозить**. future: я отвезу́ · ты отвезёшь · он отвезёт · мы отвезём · вы отвезёте · они отвезу́т. — Wiktionary, «отвезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отвозить — отвезти — to take (haul) to отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёз деньги в банк.» (I took (by vehicle) money to the bank.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **довезу** (**довезти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **привезу** (**привезти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **свезу** (**свезти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Did you bring an umbrella with you?
exercises.why: **принёс** is the past tense (masculine) of **принести** (to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приносить**. past: он принёс · она принесла́ · оно принесло́ · они принесли́. — Wiktionary, «принести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приносить — принести — to bring (on foot).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **внёс** (**внести**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **перенёс** (**перенести**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **поднёс** (**поднести**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **прошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **обошёл** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **подошёл** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **отойти** (to go away, to go aside, to move away, to move aside; (military) to withdraw, to fall back) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отходить**. past: он отошёл · она отошла́ · оно отошло́ · они отошли́. — Wiktionary, «отойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  Compare: «Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **обошёл** (**обойти**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **прошёл** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **довела** is the past tense (feminine) of **довести** (to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **доводить**. past: он довёл · она довела́ · оно довело́ · они довели́. — Wiktionary, «довести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **ввела** (**ввести**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **перевела** (**перевести**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **привела** (**привести**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **выходит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **выходить** (to go out, to come out, to walk out; to withdraw, to retire) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **выйти**. present: я выхожу́ · ты выхо́дишь · он выхо́дит · мы выхо́дим · вы выхо́дите · они выхо́дят. — Wiktionary, «выходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  The other choices: **заходит** (**заходить**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **обходит** (**обходить**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **отходит** (**отходить**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

The other choices: **выбежал** (**выбежать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **сбежал** (**сбежать**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards; **убежал** (**убежать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The plane still hasn't taken off.
exercises.why: **взлетел** is the past tense (masculine) of **взлететь** (to fly up, to soar, to take off, to take wing; (figurative) to zoom) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **взлетать**. past: он взлете́л · она взлете́ла · оно взлете́ло · они взлете́ли. — Wiktionary, «взлететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вз-, взо-, воз-, вс-, вос-** — Movement upwards. Antonym: с- Example: Альпинист взошёл на гору. — The mountain climber walked up the mountain. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **перелетел** (**перелететь**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **прилетел** (**прилететь**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion; **слетел** (**слететь**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: A sigh fell from her lips.
exercises.why: **слетел** is the past tense (masculine) of **слететь** (to fly down (from), to fly away (from); (colloquial) to fall down (from), to fall (off)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **слетать**. past: он слете́л · она слете́ла · оно слете́ло · они слете́ли. — Wiktionary, «слететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вылетел** (**вылететь**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **долетел** (**долететь**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **прилетел** (**прилететь**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: She is going to drive me crazy!
exercises.why: **сведёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **свести** (to lead, to take (from somewhere); to bring together, to throw together) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сводить**. future: я сведу́ · ты сведёшь · он сведёт · мы сведём · вы сведёте · они сведу́т. — Wiktionary, «свести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **введёт** (**ввести**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **обведёт** (**обвести**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **приведёт** (**привести**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **пришел** is the past tense (masculine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **зашёл** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **перешёл** (**перейти**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. The other choices: **заводит** (**заводить**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **отводит** (**отводить**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **переводит** (**переводить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **увезли** is the past tense (plural) of **увезти** (to take away, to carry away (by vehicle); to abduct, to kidnap) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **увозить**. past: он увёз · она увезла́ · оно увезло́ · они увезли́. — Wiktionary, «увезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «увозить — увезти — to take (haul) away.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **ввезли** (**ввезти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **отвезли** (**отвезти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **подвезли** (**подвезти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **занесло** is the past tense (neuter) of **занести** (to bring, to carry (in); to note down, to enter (data, records)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заносить**. past: он занёс · она занесла́ · оно занесло́ · они занесли́. — Wiktionary, «занести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **донесло** (**донести**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **перенесло** (**перенести**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **пронесло** (**пронести**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
